title: 1983 AHSME Problem 6
statement: When \(x^5,\) \(x+\frac1x\) and \(1+\frac2x+\frac3{x^3}\) are multiplied, the product is a polynomial of degree

solutions.text:
The greatest exponent comes from \(x^5\cdot x\cdot1=x^6.\) Every other term has smaller exponent, and the smallest possible exponent is \(5-1-3=1,\) so the product is indeed a polynomial. Its degree is \(6.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is C.
hints: Track the largest exponent produced by choosing one term from each factor
